_doc.what_this_is: A WORKED, schema-valid example of verify/run_cells.json for the toy 'city transit ridership' topic. COPY THE STRUCTURE, REPLACE THE CONTENT: it carries two PRE-TESTED runnable snippets covering BOTH grading modes — one montecarlo (reduced_n set, graded '≈ within noise') and one exact derived (reduced_n null, stdout must match byte-for-byte). Keys mirror the 'computation' entries in verify_map.example.json.
_doc.purpose: run_cells.json holds the in-browser-runnable version of each computation element in verify_map.json (same ids). The Inspector's 'Run' button executes runnable entries via a lazily-loaded Pyodide and compares stdout to expected_stdout.
_doc.self_contained: SELF-CONTAINED: every input the snippet needs is inlined as a Python literal in `code`. No file reads, no network, no dependence on other cells or page state.
_doc.pyodide_imports_only: PYODIDE-SAFE IMPORTS ONLY: numpy, pandas, and the Python standard library (math, json, itertools, collections, ...). No requests, no urllib network use, no third-party packages outside numpy/pandas.
_doc.pre_tested: PRE-TESTED: the snippet has been run and `code` reproduces `expected_stdout` exactly (byte-for-byte after normalising trailing newline). A snippet that does not reproduce its expected_stdout must not ship.
_doc.reduced_n_rule: HEAVY COMPUTE -> reduced_n: if the published figure needs a large sample (Monte-Carlo etc.), the in-browser snippet runs a SMALLER reduced_n and is graded '≈ within noise', NEVER a hard PASS. The exact, full-N version lives in the notebook (see full_ref).
_doc.this_examples_numbers: In THIS example, ana_crowd_risk runs a reduced N=10,000 -> 18.6%, within Monte-Carlo noise of the published N=200,000 figure of 18.4% (analytic 18.41%); it is graded '≈ within noise', never a hard PASS. ana_line_share is exact and must match byte-for-byte. Both were pre-tested with python 3.13; the Monte-Carlo cell seeds its RNG so it is deterministic (same output on three consecutive runs).
_doc.byte_identity: run_cells.json must be byte-identical to the inline `runCells` <script> island embedded in index.html. This file is the on-disk source of truth.

ana_crowd_risk.code:
# Estimate the chance the Red line exceeds its 195k crowding threshold on a weekday.
# Daily boardings ~ Normal(mean=182.4k, sd=14.0k), fit on the ridership log.
# Reduced N=10,000 in-browser (the published figure uses N=200,000); within Monte-Carlo noise.
import numpy as np

MEAN_K, SD_K, THRESHOLD_K = 182.4, 14.0, 195.0
N, SEED = 10000, 4326
rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)

daily = rng.normal(MEAN_K, SD_K, N)
p_over = (daily > THRESHOLD_K).mean()
print(f"Red line crowding risk (reduced Monte-Carlo, N={N:,}, seed={SEED})")
print(f"  mean weekday boardings = {MEAN_K:.1f}k, sd = {SD_K:.1f}k, threshold = {THRESHOLD_K:.0f}k")
print(f"  P(boardings > {THRESHOLD_K:.0f}k on a weekday) = {p_over*100:.1f}%")
ana_crowd_risk.expected_stdout:
Red line crowding risk (reduced Monte-Carlo, N=10,000, seed=4326)
  mean weekday boardings = 182.4k, sd = 14.0k, threshold = 195k
  P(boardings > 195k on a weekday) = 18.6%
ana_crowd_risk.note: Reduced N=10,000 in-browser -> 18.6%, within Monte-Carlo noise of the published N=200,000 figure of 18.4% (analytic P(X>195)=18.41%). Graded '≈ within noise', NOT a hard PASS.
ana_crowd_risk.full_ref: code/build_crowding.py (N=200,000, seed=4326) reproduces forecast_outputs/crowding.json exactly; the notebook cell cell_crowding (verify/transit_forecast.ipynb) runs the full-N version.

ana_line_share.code:
import pandas as pd
# Inlined from ridership.csv: average weekday boardings per line (thousands).
df = pd.DataFrame(
    [["Red", 182.4], ["Blue", 131.0], ["Green", 96.6],
     ["Gold", 58.2], ["Silver", 40.8]],
    columns=["line", "weekday_boardings_k"])
total = df["weekday_boardings_k"].sum()
df["share_pct"] = (df["weekday_boardings_k"] / total * 100).round(1)
df = df.sort_values("weekday_boardings_k", ascending=False)
print("Average weekday boardings by line (thousands) and share of the network:")
for _, r in df.iterrows():
    print(f"  {r.line:7} {r.weekday_boardings_k:6.1f}k  {r.share_pct:5.1f}%")
top = df.iloc[0]
print(f"network total = {total:.1f}k weekday boardings")
print(f"busiest line = {top.line} at {top.share_pct:.1f}% of the network")
